summary: A full-scope import reconciliation and Part II of the current upstream smooth-representation roadmap. Existing upstream targets and the two atlas parts are referenced under their existing identifiers, never copied into new nodes. New targets are the compact-section cosheaf, the Schwartz-algebra route to tempered Ext vanishing, principal-series centre completions and their tangent maps, and a precise finite-central-algebra interface. The late integral finiteness and second-adjointness chain retains its existing target identifiers and explicit geometric prerequisites. Complete means the target-level planning pass is complete, not that all mathematics is implemented or all gaps are resolved.

nodes.title: The compact-section cosheaf
nodes.statement: For a Hausdorff locally compact totally disconnected space X, a commutative ring A and an A-module M with the discrete topology, equip U ↦ C_c^∞(U,M), on open subsets of X, with extension-by-zero maps. For every open cover U=⋃ᵢ Uᵢ the sequence ⊕ᵢⱼ C_c^∞(Uᵢ∩Uⱼ,M) → ⊕ᵢ C_c^∞(Uᵢ,M) → C_c^∞(U,M) → 0 is right exact, where the first map is the difference of the two extension maps. Construct the natural isomorphism B⊗_A C_c^∞(U,M) ≅ C_c^∞(U,B⊗_A M) for every A-algebra B; no flatness is required.
hypotheses: X is Hausdorff, locally compact and totally disconnected.
M is an algebraic module, given the discrete topology only to express local constancy.
The cosheaf uses extension by zero on compact supports; it does not glue arbitrary noncompact sections.
proofSteps: Use the imported finite disjoint compact-open expansion and common-refinement theorem for compact sections.
Refine the compact support by finitely many compact opens subordinate to the cover; extend each indicator by zero.
For a relation between presentations, take a common finite disjoint refinement. Each resulting relation lies in a pairwise intersection.
On each finite disjoint partition the coefficient-change map is the finite direct-sum tensor isomorphism. Pass through refinements and filtered unions.

sources.match: The existing indicator expansion and common refinement supply the carrier and the finite gluing argument; the cosheaf and arbitrary module coefficient-change API extend those targets.

Integral compact-section and Haar conventions fix the setting. The module-valued cosheaf is deduced here from the imported compact-open partition theorem, rather than attributed as a theorem of this paper.

acceptance: All sums in a single section or relation have finite support, even for an infinite cover.
The coefficient-change isomorphism sends b⊗(1_K m) to 1_K(b⊗m).

nodes.title: The Harish–Chandra Schwartz algebra
nodes.statement: For G the rational points of a connected reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field, over C, fix Haar measure, a good base point x₀ in the enlarged building, the proper length σ(g)=d(gx₀,x₀), and Harish–Chandra’s positive spherical function Ξ normalized by Ξ(1)=1. For each compact open K define S(G,K) to be the bi-K-invariant complex functions f for which sup_g |f(g)| Ξ(g)⁻¹(1+σ(g))ⁿ is finite for every n≥0. With convolution these are Fréchet algebras. Define S(G)=⋃_K S(G,K), with its inductive-limit topology and the imported Hecke idempotents as local units. Supply the injective convolution homomorphism H(G,C)→S(G) and the canonical S(G,K)=e_K S(G)e_K comparison.
hypotheses: G is connected reductive over a nonarchimedean local field; Haar measure is the same measure as for the imported complex Hecke algebra.
σ is proper on the building directions including the split central factor; Ξ uses normalized unitary induction from a minimal parabolic and the normalized spherical vector.
This Schwartz algebra is a completion of the Hecke algebra, distinct from the mirabolic Schwartz submodule in SR.5.
proofSteps: Construct σ from the supplied enlarged building and Ξ from the spherical matrix coefficient in normalized unitary induction.
Prove the Harish–Chandra estimates needed for convolution and completeness on each K-corner.
Compare nested K-corners and form their directed union; transfer the normalized Hecke idempotents.
Prove independence of auxiliary good points and equivalent proper lengths by comparison of the defining seminorms.

sources.match: The Schwartz algebra is the union of its Fréchet compact-open corners. The stated seminorm model requires Harish–Chandra estimates, recorded as a gap rather than inferred from compact convolution.
The nondegenerate Schwartz-module category and its local units are the algebraic setting for the discrete-component argument.

acceptance: The inclusion preserves the convolution order fixed in SR.1.
Changing the length to an equivalent proper length gives the same locally convex algebra.

nodes.title: Tempered Schwartz modules
nodes.statement: Define Mod(S(G)) to be the category of algebraic nondegenerate left S(G)-modules: each vector is fixed by some e_K. Restriction along H(G,C)→S(G) gives a smooth G-representation. For an admissible smooth representation V with scalar central character ω, prove that the imported matrix-coefficient temperedness predicate holds if and only if its H(G,C)-action extends to S(G). For any admissible V, prove uniqueness when such an extension exists. The category itself includes modules without a scalar central character. Keep algebraic modules distinct from Fréchet, LF and bornological module categories; the Ext target here is the algebraic category.
hypotheses: Use the complex Schwartz algebra just constructed.

Comparison with the imported matrix-coefficient predicate requires admissible V with scalar central character ω; temperedness includes unitarity of ω. Uniqueness of extension requires admissibility but not a scalar central character.
Exactness in the algebraic module category is exactness of underlying modules; no topological splitting is built into it.
proofSteps: Apply the imported locally unital-module construction to S(G) and its e_K.
Recover the smooth action from the nondegenerate H(G,C)-restriction.
Establish the admissible temperedness/extension comparison using the Schwartz continuity estimates; do not define temperedness by an assumed extension.

acceptance: Restriction is exact and sends e_KV to V^K.

The imported temperedness comparison retains admissibility and a scalar central character; the algebraic category and its Ext comparison impose neither a scalar central character nor unitarizability on every object.

nodes.title: Schwartz comparison resolutions
nodes.statement: For an admissible complex S(G)-module V and a sufficiently small good compact open K, the Schneider–Stuhler coefficient-system complex on the enlarged Bruhat–Tits building gives a projective resolution of V^K as an H(G,K)-module. Its scalar extension to S(G,K) is the corresponding completed coefficient-system resolution and has the continuous contracting homotopy of Opdam–Solleveld. The finite-generation and continuity properties identify algebraic Hom into arbitrary S(G,K)-modules with the required comparison complex.
hypotheses: K is in the good cofinal family of Opdam–Solleveld, not an arbitrary compact open.
V is admissible and generated by V^K; refine K until the relevant Bernstein component is generated at that level.
The group has the enlarged affine building and coefficient systems of ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2.
proofSteps: Construct the cellular coefficient system from compact-open invariant spaces on facets.
Use the augmented building contraction and the Schneider–Stuhler exactness theorem to obtain the Hecke resolution.
Extend the contraction with the decay estimates to the Schwartz corners, preserving the augmentation.
Check the finite-generation and good-level hypotheses used to identify the Hom complexes.

nodes.title: Tempered Ext comparison
nodes.statement: For V,W nondegenerate algebraic S(G)-modules with V admissible, restriction gives natural isomorphisms Extⁿ_H(G)(V,W) ≅ Extⁿ_S(G)(V,W) for every n≥0. Identify the first group with Ext in smooth complex G-representations using the imported Hecke-module equivalence. If both modules are generated at a sufficiently small good compact open K, also identify these groups with the corresponding corner Ext groups. Topological Ext comparisons require the additional LF or Fréchet hypotheses and are not needed for the present application.
hypotheses: Complex coefficients.
V is admissible; W need not be admissible for the algebraic comparison.
Both modules carry actual S(G)-actions, not just arbitrarily chosen collections of tempered constituents.
proofSteps: Decompose both module categories by the imported central Bernstein idempotents; the decomposition persists to Ext. In each component choose a good level generating that whole component, without asserting a single global level for arbitrary admissible V.
Use the comparison resolutions to identify Hom complexes in the Hecke and Schwartz categories.
Pass to cohomology componentwise and transport across the exact locally unital-module equivalence.
Check naturality, including degree zero, before passing between good corners.

sources.match: The algebraic Ext comparison assumes the source is admissible; the statement also separates the extra topological comparisons.

acceptance: In degree zero the isomorphism is the actual restriction map on equivariant morphisms.
No general flatness of S(G) over H(G) is asserted.

nodes.title: Discrete-series tempered projectivity
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive with compact centre, and let δ be an irreducible complex discrete-series representation. Then δ is projective as a nondegenerate S(G)-module. Consequently Extⁿ_smooth(G)(δ,W)=0 for every n>0 and every nondegenerate S(G)-module W. In particular this vanishing applies when W is an irreducible admissible tempered representation, as in Gan–Savin Proposition 5.3. No projectivity in the entire smooth category is asserted.
hypotheses: The centre is compact; for noncompact centre an individual unitary unramified character can have self-extensions.
δ is irreducible, unitary and square-integrable modulo the centre.
Complex coefficients; W carries the Schwartz action.
proofSteps: Use Schneider–Zink Proposition 2.3 to split δ into finitely many copies of the Schwartz algebra of G⁰, where G⁰ is generated by compact open subgroups.

The structure recalled in Schneider–Zink §2, p. 5 gives G/G⁰ free abelian and G⁰Z of finite index for the maximal split central torus Z. Compact centre makes Z trivial, so this quotient is both finite and free abelian and G⁰=G. Thus the splitting gives projectivity over S(G).
Apply the admissible-source Ext comparison to transfer the vanishing to smooth representations.
For G₂(F), use compactness of its centre and the already supplied discrete-series status of the representation in the downstream application.

sources.match: Projectivity over S(G⁰) is explicit. When unramified characters vary in a positive-dimensional torus, the projective object is the whole family, so the compact-centre hypothesis must be retained.
The Ext comparison transfers Schwartz projectivity to Ext against Schwartz modules.
The application kills the discrete-series contribution to Ext¹ against an irreducible tempered target.

acceptance: For G=SL₂(F), this gives Ext¹(St,π)=0 for every irreducible tempered π.
For G=F× the compact-centre hypothesis fails: χ⊗(1+ε·v_F) gives a nontrivial smooth self-extension of a unitary character, so that false generalization is rejected.

nodes.title: The principal-series Bernstein centre over E
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite and E/Q_p sufficiently large for the character data and the Bernstein component. Fix n≥1 and smooth E-valued characters φ₁,…,φₙ of K×. Let D be the torus component containing their tensor product, and Ω the corresponding principal-series component of GLₙ(K). Construct the E-form of the imported Bernstein block and its centre H, identifying H with H_D^W(D), where H_D is the coordinate algebra of the torus of unramified twists of this fixed inertial character datum and W(D) stabilizes its inertial class. Each GL₁ coordinate centre H_i is a one-variable Laurent algebra; Spec H_i is G_m, rather than the algebra H_i itself. Use the affine Weyl action determined by the chosen base characters when their inertial restrictions coincide.
hypotheses: E contains the values needed to define the compact character data and the finite Weyl twists, as in CEGGPS §3.13.
The character data and a square root of q used for normalized induction are defined over E.
Only the split principal-series block is extended from the upstream complex theory; arbitrary E-forms of all Bernstein blocks are not new targets here.
proofSteps: Use compact induction of the torus inertial character to identify its centre with the unramified character coordinate algebra.
Use the imported block/projective-generator construction over a splitting field, then faithfully flat descent to E.
Identify the GLₙ block centre with invariants under the inertial stabilizer, including the character twists in its action.
Identify the coordinate centres with Laurent algebras after choosing the valuation generator; record how changing that choice transports the coordinates.

The smooth principal-series representation and its individual GL₁ Bernstein centres supply the application.

acceptance: The centre is the actual categorical centre of Ω_E, not a chosen ring of scalar parameters.
For pairwise different inertial restrictions, W(D) is trivial; for repeated restrictions its affine action is retained.

nodes.title: Ordered characters and the Bernstein spectrum
nodes.statement: In the preceding principal-series setting define η=1⊠|·|_K⊠⋯⊠|·|_K^(n−1), and w(φ)_i=φ_(w⁻¹i). For each permutation w construct J_w: X_w=∏ᵢ Spec H_(w⁻¹i)→Spec H by the central character of the unnormalized lower-Borel induction Ind_(B⁻)^(GLₙ(K))(w(φ′)η). This is the finite torus-to-invariant-quotient morphism, transported by the fixed normalizing twist. If p_(w₂,w₁):X_w₁→X_w₂ reorders by w₂w₁⁻¹, the typed equality is J_w₂∘p_(w₂,w₁)=J_w₁. Record the contravariant equality on coordinate-algebra maps.
hypotheses: All inertial character data are fixed, and φ′ varies only through their unramified twists.
η and the lower Borel are fixed; this is Ding’s unnormalized induction convention.
An assertion about irreducibility is restricted to the generic locus φ_i/φ_j≠1,|·|_K for all i≠j.
proofSteps: Use the invariant-subring inclusion to construct the finite affine quotient map.
Identify its closed-point central character by the imported principal-series induction and Bernstein action, with η included.
Construct the source reorderings and check the equality before passing to points, completions or tangent spaces.

nodes.title: Completed principal-series centres
nodes.statement: Assume the generic smooth tuple φ satisfies φ_i/φ_j≠1,|·|_K for every i≠j, and E contains its point coordinates. At x_w=w(φ)∈X_w and z=J_w(x_w), pullback induces an isomorphism of complete local E-algebras Ĥ_z≅Ô_(X_w,x_w). The latter represents unramified deformations of the ordered characters with fixed compact restrictions, and is a power-series algebra over E in n variables after choosing local coordinates. These isomorphisms are compatible with source reorderings. They are local statements at the specified generic points, not global isomorphisms of the ordered torus and Bernstein quotient.
hypotheses: K/Q_p finite; n≥1; E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p.
The tuple is generic as above; in particular no nontrivial inertial Weyl element fixes its full character point.
Completions are at the specified E-rational maximal ideals.
proofSteps: Use the principal-series centre as a finite invariant quotient.
Show the stabilizer of the generic ordered point is trivial: a fixing permutation would equate two full characters.
Apply the finite free-orbit quotient/completion theorem over characteristic zero and the equality of residue fields.
Identify the ordered-character completion and transport the source-permutation identity through completion.

sources.match: The completed Bernstein centre is identified with the formal unramified character-deformation ring. The generic tuple and the source map are fixed in §3.1.1 and Proposition 3.3.
The torus invariant quotient is the input; local étaleness at a free orbit is the additional commutative-algebra interface requested here.

acceptance: For GL₁, the completed local ring of E[T,T⁻¹] at T=a≠0 is E[[u]] with u=T/a−1.

nodes.title: Smooth tangent and extension parameters
nodes.statement: For the generic tuple and smooth irreducible π_sm=Ind_(B⁻)(φ η), identify the tangent space at each ordered-character point with Hom_sm(T(K),E), of dimension n, by φ_i↦φ_i(1+εψ_i). The tangent of J_w identifies this space with the tangent of the completed block centre and with Ext¹ in the smooth E-linear representation category of π_sm by itself. For p_(w₂,w₁) the resulting maps satisfy ζ_w₂∘d p_(w₂,w₁)=ζ_w₁. This is the smooth part of Ding’s comparison; locally analytic central-character directions and the dimension n+[K:Q_p] are owned by the locally analytic roadmap.
hypotheses: K/Q_p finite; φ generic; E sufficiently large; π_sm and its central character are E-rational.
Hom_sm denotes additive homomorphisms with open kernel; each K× factor therefore contributes its valuation direction.
Self-extension classes are in the smooth category; arbitrary locally analytic extensions are excluded from this target.
proofSteps: Describe smooth first-order deformations of the coordinate characters by their additive open-kernel logarithmic derivatives.
Use the imported exact Jacquet/induction APIs on the generic principal-series block to identify first-order smooth deformations and self-extensions.
